title: doppeldata scenario
description: A scenario file: a layer over a profile that bends the generated data on purpose.

expect.description: What the scenario promises of the generated data, which `data check --scenario` certifies.

perturbations.description:
Faults applied in order to each block of generated rows. Each draws from its own stream,
keyed by its `id`, so inserting one never moves another's rows.

table.description:
The table of a bundle the scenario bends: its patch and every perturbation apply to that table
alone. A bundle takes only a scenario naming one of its tables.

type.description: An Arrow type string, as a profile's `physical_type` spells it.

CdcStyle.description: Which tool's layout a change stream takes.

oneOf.description: AWS DMS writing to Amazon S3: `LOAD` files, then timestamp-named change files.

CdcTimestampUnit.description: The unit DMS stores Parquet timestamps at: `ms` with `ParquetTimestampInMillisecond`, else `us`.

oneOf.description: 1, 2, 3 and on, each `1 − 1/mean` as likely as the one before.

CountSpread.description: A count of one or more, drawn from a family by its mean.

DateDelimiter.description: What separates a folder name's date parts, as DMS's `DatePartitionDelimiter` names it.

oneOf.description: One folder per part, as `2026/10/01/`.

DatePartition.description:
Change files filed under folders named for their commit date, as DMS's `DatePartitionEnabled`
files them. Full-load files are never partitioned.

DateSequence.description: The date parts a folder is named for, in order, as DMS's `DatePartitionSequence` names them.

oneOf.description: Each copy is written to the file its source row is written to.
Each copy comes from a block half the dataset away, so from another file.

Duration.description: A length of time as a whole number above zero and a unit: ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as 2d.

Expectation.description: A statistic the scenario promises of the generated data, within its bounds.

column.description: The column measured. A metric of the whole table, such as `malformed.fraction`, takes none.

ExpectedMetric.description: The statistics an expectation can name. Each is measured on the generated data.

oneOf.description:
The share of rows holding the `keys` most frequent values of `column`, with `keys` from the
column's `hot_keys` perturbation.

The share of rows whose `column`, a key each copy shares with its source, repeats an earlier
row's. A later perturbation writing that column is refused, because a copy's key would then
differ from its source's.

The share of rows whose `column` is earlier than the `ingest` column of its `late_arrival`
perturbation.
The share of rows whose `column` is null, the profile's own nulls included.

The share of a CSV or TSV dataset's data rows a reader rejects, as a profile's
`source.csv.malformed.fraction` records it. It takes no column.

FaultKind.description: One way a file is broken. A row kind breaks one record, and a file kind a whole file.

oneOf.description: A record ending before its last 1 to n − 1 fields.
A record carrying 1 or 2 fields past the last.
A lone quote inside a quoted field.
A line break inside a quoted string field, which is legal CSV.
`N/A`, `-`, `?` or a unit suffix in place of a typed value, or text of another type.
A lone continuation byte or the bytes C3 28 inside a field.
A record past DuckDB's default `max_line_size`.
The file's last record cut mid-field, with no line break, as a cut-off upload leaves it.
A file starting with the UTF-8 byte order mark.
A file whose records end in LF, CRLF and CR mixed.
A file written with another delimiter than the rest.
A file whose header renames a column or swaps two, its values swapped with it.
A file encoded windows-1252 among UTF-8 ones.
A JSON array among NDJSON files, or an NDJSON file among JSON arrays.
A record missing its closing brace.
A number or boolean written as a string.
A file whose timestamp columns are stored at another unit than the rest.
A file whose timestamp columns are stored as INT96, as Hive and Impala wrote them.
A file whose decimal columns are stored one digit of scale wider than the rest.

LagSpread.description: How far a late row's time moves, as a lognormal by its median and 99th percentile.

p99.description:
Without it, the lognormal's sigma is 1, which puts the 99th percentile about ten times the
median.

oneOf.description: Missing completely at random.
Missing at random, given another column.
Missing not at random: the column's own value decides.

Period.description: The span the changes are committed across.

start.description: The full load's time, which every commit falls after.

Perturbation.description:
One fault, named by `op`. `id` keys its random stream, and defaults to
`<op>:<column or "table">:<n>`, where n counts earlier entries of the same op and column.

oneOf.description:
`fraction` of rows take one of `keys` values: the column's most frequent ones, or values its own
sampler draws where it lists none.

Copies of existing rows, so that `fraction` of the rows written are copies. Each block's count is
planned up front, so block boundaries never move.

exact.description: False varies one non-key column of each copy, taking that column's value from another row.

oneOf.description: `fraction` of rows have their event time shifted earlier by a drawn lag.

ingest.description:
A column to hold each row's unshifted time, as when it arrived. It is written whether or not
the profile holds it, and added with the event column's type when it does not. A date
column takes the time truncated to its day. `late_arrival.fraction` is measured against it.

oneOf.description:
Nulls written into `column`: MCAR uniformly, MAR more often for higher values of `depends_on`,
and MNAR more often for the column's own higher values. Each averages `fraction` over the rows.

depends_on.description: The column MAR's chance of a null rises with. Only MAR takes it.

oneOf.description:
`fraction` of rows take a sentinel from `values`, or a value past the column's extreme on the side
`beyond` names. Exactly one of the two is given.

values.description: Sentinels, each cast to the column's type.

oneOf.description: Two columns' values exchanged in `fraction` of rows. Both must have one type.

The category mix moved: each value named takes its share, and every other value keeps its
proportion of what is left. As few rows change as reach the new mix.
Gaussian noise of standard deviation `sigma`, in the column's units, added to `fraction` of rows.
`fraction` of rows multiplied by `factor`, a unit error such as cents written as dollars.

`fraction` of strings broken: one holding a character past ASCII is mojibake, its UTF-8 read as
windows-1252, and any other has one character replaced by U+FFFD.

`fraction` of rows set far past the trimmed extremes: between `multiplier` and `multiplier + 1`
times the span between them, beyond the high extreme, or beyond the low one in a column that
goes below zero.

Files whose first row lies at or past `after_fraction` of the rows carry a new shape. Every
name but `add`'s and `reorder`'s is a column as the profile names it.

add.description: Columns that appear, generated from their type alone.

reorder.description:
Columns moved to the front in this order, by the names they end with. The rest follow in
their order.

widen.description: Columns cast to a wider Arrow type, such as int32 to int64.

oneOf.description:
File sizes drawn from `file_rows` in place of the layout's. A caller's own file size still
overrides it.

Each value named takes its share of rows, written as the column's type. Every other row keeps
its own value, so a partitioned write's directories hold those shares.

Bytes a reader rejects or misreads, written into the files and listed in `_faults.jsonl` beside
them. With no `fraction`, `kinds` or `files_fraction`, it reproduces the malformed rows and type mix
the profile records of its CSV source. Otherwise `fraction` of rows each take one of the row
kinds named, and `files_fraction` of files each take one of the file kinds named.

files_fraction.description: The share of files given a file fault, each kind named equally often.

fraction.description: The share of rows given a row fault, each kind named equally often.

oneOf.description:
A change stream in the layout a change-data-capture tool writes, beside `_expected`, the table a
correct merge of it produces. The full load is the table the profile generates. The changes are
drawn across `period`, each commit time after its start, so the same seed writes the same
bytes on any day.

date_partition.description: Without it, every change file lies directly under the prefix.

delete_fraction.description: The share of the full load's rows deleted, each after its updates.

duplicate_delivery_fraction.description:
The chance an eligible change is written a second time, in the first change file after the
one holding its key's last change. A change is eligible when its key's last change comes
after it, and deletes the row or leaves it different from this change's.

file_interval.description: One change file per interval with any changes. Without it, `1m`, as DMS's `CdcMaxBatchInterval`.

include_op_for_full_load.description: Write `I` as the first field of every full-load record, as DMS's `IncludeOpForFullLoad` does.

insert_fraction.description: New rows, as a share of the full load's.

key.description:
The key column, which every change of a row holds as it is. Without it, the profile's
`dataset.keys.primary`, which must name one column.

out_of_order_fraction.description:
The chance an eligible change is written late instead, in the first change file after the
one holding its key's last change. Eligible as for `duplicate_delivery_fraction`.

schema.description: The schema in the `<schema>/<table>/` prefix every file is written under.

timestamp_column.description:
The column holding each record's commit time, as DMS's `TimestampColumnName` names it.
Without it, `dms_commit_ts`.

timestamp_unit.description: The unit every timestamp column of a Parquet write is stored at. Without it, `us`.

update_fraction.description: The share of the full load's rows updated at least once.

updates_per_row.description: How many times an updated row is updated. Without it, once.

ProfilePatch.description: An RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch onto the profile. `columns` is a map keyed by column name, an extension of RFC 7396, whose arrays replace wholesale, so a patch names only the columns it changes. A column patched to null is removed, and one the profile does not hold is refused. In a bundle, `relationships` is a map keyed by the `from` columns of each relationship drawing a column of the scenario's table, joined by `,` and without their table, such as `customer_id`.

RowsSpread.description: A count of rows, as a lognormal by its median and 99th percentile.

p99.description:
Without it, the lognormal's sigma is 1, which puts the 99th percentile about ten times the
median.

UtcInstant.description: An instant in RFC 3339, such as 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z.
